replies.text: {"verdicts":[{"id":"T1","keep":true,"reason":"Design states agent attaches drive files mentioned in email and invites named people; concrete exfiltration attack."},{"id":"T2","keep":true,"reason":"Prompt injection steering agent goals via email body is a distinct attack on the email-driven task path."},{"id":"T3","keep":true,"reason":"Broad standing inbox/calendar/drive access supported by quotes; privilege scoping concern specific to this agent."},{"id":"T4","keep":true,"reason":"Spoofed sender/attendee names trusted for invites sent under employee identity; distinct spoofing attack."},{"id":"T5","keep":true,"reason":"Persistent poisoned inbox context affecting later unrelated requests is a distinct attack from direct injection."},{"id":"T6","keep":true,"reason":"Design explicitly says agent acts without asking; attribution gap for invites and file shares is specific."},{"id":"T7","keep":true,"reason":"Email trigger reachable by anyone; flooding causes calendar spam and cost, tied to stated booking behaviour."},{"id":"T8","keep":true,"reason":"Reconnaissance harvesting valid addresses and free/busy via invite replies is a different harm than file exfiltration."}]}
